Medical History

- Current health concerns and risk factors: New left elbow swelling noticed about 1 week ago; not painful but area is slightly warm with a sense of fluid inside. Patient able to move elbow normally. History of osteoarthritis. Active lifestyle (runs 2–3 times per week). Peanut allergy. Not on regular medications.
- Relevant family medical history: Not documented clearly; patient could not confirm rheumatologic diseases in family; OA in patient noted.
- Medications (including OTC or shared medications): Not on regular medications. Ibuprofen 400 mg PO twice daily after meals recommended (dose documented in plan). Allergy to peanuts noted.

Assessment & Plan (Integrating DDx)

- Working diagnosis: Olecranon bursitis (aseptic/inflammatory) of the left elbow.
- Supporting context from transcript and consistency with DDx: Swelling localized to the elbow with mild warmth, preserved range of motion, no acute trauma, and clinical assessment favoring bursitis. Plan includes NSAID therapy and a comprehensive blood test panel to evaluate inflammatory/infectious/autoimmune etiologies and gout. Not currently septic arthritis; patient advised to seek urgent care if redness, rapid progression, or severe pain develops.
- Differential diagnoses considered (consistent with DDx, aligned with transcript): 
  - Osteoarthritis with elbow effusion (Medium likelihood) given history of OA and age.
  - Inflammatory/autoimmune arthritis (Medium) due to joint swelling and planned rheumatologic serology.
  - Crystal arthropathy (gout/CPPD) (Medium) due to possible inflammatory arthritis and planned urate/CPPD assessment.
  - Septic arthritis (Low) but remains a critical red flag to monitor; patient advised on urgent evaluation if red flags develop.
- Plan summary: Order blood tests for inflammatory markers, infection, rheumatologic antibodies, and gout; follow-up appointment to review results (in clinic or by telehealth). Continue NSAID therapy (ibuprofen 400 mg PO twice daily after meals; discontinue if heartburn occurs). Reassess after blood test results; urgent reassessment if symptoms worsen.

Management Plan

- Medications: Ibuprofen 400 mg orally twice daily after meals; discontinue if heartburn develops.
- Investigations: Blood test forms to be mailed for inflammatory markers, infectious/inflammatory autoimmune antibodies, and gout-related tests; results in ~5–6 days; follow-up to review results (in person or via telehealth).
- Follow-up: Arrange a follow-up appointment to assess elbow and review blood test results; option for telephone or video follow-up if convenient; patient to contact clinic sooner if symptoms worsen or red flags develop.
- Education/monitoring: Monitor for increasing redness, warmth spreading beyond elbow, significant pain, fever, or reduced elbow function; seek urgent care if these occur.

Consider:

- Allied health referral (EPC – 10 visits): Not recorded.
- Reproductive or sexual health clinic referral: Not recorded.
- Mental health support if indicated: Not recorded.
- CTG registration: Not recorded.
- Preventive health follow-up booked (e.g., flu vaccine, Pap test): Not recorded.

Summary of Differential Diagnoses (from DDx)

- Olecranon bursitis (aseptic) of the left elbow
  - Likelihood: High
  - Justification: Localized swelling with mild warmth, preserved motion, absence of acute systemic illness; clinician explicitly entertained bursitis and treated accordingly.
- Osteoarthritis with elbow effusion
  - Likelihood: Moderate
  - Justification: Known OA history and age; OA can be associated with joint swelling.
- Inflammatory/autoimmune arthritis (e.g., rheumatoid arthritis or reactive arthritis)
  - Likelihood: Moderate
  - Justification: Elbow swelling with inflammatory potential; rheumatologic serology planned.
- Crystal arthropathy (gout or CPPD)
  - Likelihood: Moderate
  - Justification: Plan to screen for gout/CPPD; age-compatible but elbow involvement is less typical for gout.
- Septic arthritis
  - Likelihood: Low
  - Justification: Currently no signs of acute infection or severe redness; risk remains and patient advised on red flags.

Quality checks

- Missing but clinically expected elements: Blood pressure, BMI, immunisation status, comprehensive mental health screening, alcohol/tobacco history, sexual health history, and detailed family history beyond OA are not recorded in the transcript.
- Internal contradictions: None identified between transcript and DDx; data are aligned (bursitis favored, with broad differential due to single joint swelling and warmth).
- Transcript quality: Clear but limited vitals and some minor repetition; overall sufficient to support assessment and plan.

End of note.
